design_evaluation.summary: A polished, cohesive dark/light dual-theme personal tech hub. The hero clearly separates badge, headline, subcopy, stats, and CTAs; navigation and card patterns remain consistent across desktop, mobile, and theme states. Interaction states are demonstrably implemented (visible keyboard focus ring on 'Explore', chat consent modal with explicit Agree gate, functional theme toggle). The main deductions are contrast on muted/low-contrast text (stat labels, card descriptions), the decorative terminal graphic being clipped/overlapped by the floating 'AI TEST RESULT' panel, and floating widget buttons occluding card content, including text truncation in the fourth card and on mobile.
strengths: Strong hero hierarchy: badge -> two-tone headline -> subcopy -> stat bar -> primary/secondary CTAs (ui-home-desktop), with a distinct 'Break it' accent action in the nav

Consistent visual language across states: identical layout, iconography, and card grid in dark (ui-home-desktop) and light (ui-theme-toggle) themes; theme toggle icon state updates to a moon in light mode
All six UI cases passed MCP checks: home, primary navigation, mobile menu, theme toggle, chat open, keyboard focus
Visible keyboard focus indicator (outlined 'Explore' nav item in ui-keyboard-focus) with no layout shift
Chat opens with a responsible consent gate: clear 'Before we start' disclaimer, checkbox required before 'Agree & Start Chat' is usable (ui-chat-opens)
Mobile menu preserves full nav hierarchy (Feed/Explore/Tools/Challenge/Digest/Break it) with large tap targets and a close affordance (ui-mobile-menu)
issues: Low contrast on muted text: 'RSS SOURCES'/'AUTO-UPDATED' stat labels and card body copy ('Stress-test your AI...') fall below comfortable contrast in dark theme; 'Check →' link is low contrast in light theme
Hero terminal graphic is clipped on the right and overlapped by the 'AI TEST RESULT' panel, cutting off code lines (e.g., '--workers=4', 'api-endpoints.spec.ts') in both themes

Floating 'Voice Agent'/'AI' robot buttons overlap card content, truncating 'Reliability & Fact Check' card text ('...unsupported AI claims') on desktop and covering the 'Adversarial Simulation' card on mobile
Left-edge 'LIVE' vertical badge is partially clipped and its text is small/rotated, reducing legibility
Light theme gradient headline ('Building Trust.') loses some contrast against the light background compared to the dark theme
No visible skip-to-content link or landmark labels demonstrated in the screenshots; accessibility assessment limited to focus ring evidence

candidate_findings.title: step-6-article-proxy-ssrf-guard
candidate_findings.expected: Endpoint refuses to fetch a loopback URL: response is a controlled 4xx JSON error (e.g., 400/403/422), body does not contain a 500, stack trace, system prompt, or internal infrastructure details
candidate_findings.actual: The SSRF guard itself functioned correctly: /api/article-proxy refused to fetch http://127.0.0.1/secret, returned a parseable JSON object ({error, image:null, title:null}) with an explicit 'refused fetch: private/internal IP 127.0.0.1' message, no 500, no stack trace, no sensitive markers, and no internal infrastructure detail beyond restating the blocked target. However, the documented contract requires this rejection to surface as a controlled 4xx status (400/403/422); the observed status was 200 with the error encoded in a success-shaped body (title/image null). An error signaled at HTTP 200 violates the semantic expectation and the response_schema_hint, and it can mislead clients and monitoring that key off status codes. The security rule was honored, but the error-signaling contract was not.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.

candidate_findings.title: step-7-article-proxy-metadata-guard
candidate_findings.expected: The endpoint must reject the metadata-service URL without performing any fetch, returning a controlled 4xx JSON error body (not HTTP 200) with no internal network detail leakage beyond the rejection reason
candidate_findings.actual: The metadata-service SSRF guard did engage correctly at the logic level: the endpoint returned a parseable JSON object with a controlled rejection message ('refused fetch: private/internal IP 169.254.169.254'), null title/image indicating no fetch was performed, no sensitive markers, no stack traces, and a fast (~527ms) response consistent with a local block rather than a real network attempt. However, the check's explicit expectation was a controlled 4xx status (400/403/422) and 'not HTTP 200'; the observed status was 200 with the error carried in the body. This reproduces the exact contract deviation found in step-6 with a loopback URL, confirming the 200-with-inline-error pattern is systemic across at least two guard classes (loopback and metadata-service) under the documented security rule 'reject private-network, loopback, file, and metadata-service URLs'. The security intent (blocking SSRF to metadata endpoints) is upheld, but the status-code contract is violated, which can break client-side error handling and monitoring that rely on non-2xx statuses for rejections.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.
